title: Short Stuff: Paprika
summary: Short Stuff episode on paprika. Josh and Chuck cover what paprika is (a ground long red Capsicum annuum pepper), its association with Hungary and Spain/Portugal, its native origin in Mexico and Central America and spread to Hungary via the Balkans, and why Hungary adopted it as a national spice (abundance and lower cost). They discuss Hungarian dishes paprikash and goulash, Nancy Waldeck's comments on smoked Spanish and Portuguese paprika, and the four official Hungarian grades (Special, Gourmet, Noble, Rose) with their fineness, heat and color. They note paprika is not the same as chili powder, advise on storage since it goes stale and turns brown, and suggest trying new recipes such as paprikash, goulash and Romesco sauce.

segments.title: Opening banter and what paprika is
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode and asks whether listeners like paprika. He explains paprika is made from a long, bright red pepper of the Capsicum annuum variety, with flavors ranging from hot to sweet to smoky, and that it is big in Central Europe, Spain and Portugal.

segments.title: Origins of paprika and Hungary's adoption
segments.summary: Paprika is native to Mexico and Central America and reached Hungary through the Balkans, where it grew abundantly. Because it was plentiful and inexpensive, Hungary built much of its cooking around it, making it the national spice. Nancy Waldeck notes that paprikash and goulash remain the main Hungarian dishes using it.

segments.title: Smoked paprika in Spain and Portugal
segments.summary: Nancy Waldeck says Spanish and Portuguese paprika is so commonly smoked that labels do not mention it. Josh and Chuck discuss personal experiences, including a trip to Budapest.

segments.title: Hungarian paprika grades
segments.summary: There are about twenty varieties of paprika on shelves, but only four official Hungarian grades: Special, Gourmet, Noble and Rose. Special is very fine, sweet and mild, and the kind typically sold in the US. Gourmet is slightly coarse and can be hot or mild. Noble is a coarse grind, light red. Rose is dark red and can be very hot, with a bell-pepper taste.

segments.title: Paprika is not chili powder; storage and recipes
segments.summary: Paprika is distinct from chili powder, which is a blend of chilies, cumin and garlic, and cannot substitute for paprika. Paprika's natural oils make it go stale, so it should be stored in a dark, cool jar away from heat. The hosts encourage trying new recipes such as paprikash, goulash and Romesco sauce.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck encourage listeners to buy paprika and try something new, then close the Short Stuff episode with the standard credits.
